notes.summary: Blood relation questions describe family links in words, codes or by "pointing to a person". Draw a small family tree and you will rarely go wrong. About 1 question in Tier 1.

concepts.title: Draw a family tree
concepts.body: Use + for male and − for female, a horizontal line for married couples, a vertical line for parent–child, and a dashed line for siblings. Fill in one statement at a time.

concepts.title: Key terms
concepts.body: Father's or mother's brother = uncle. Mother's brother = maternal uncle. Son's wife = daughter-in-law. Daughter's husband = son-in-law. Wife's brother = brother-in-law.

concepts.title: Pointing questions
concepts.body: Start from the end of the sentence ("my father's only son" = me, if I am male) and work back to the person pointed at.

varieties.name: Pointing / introducing
varieties.how: Break the sentence from "my …" and simplify step by step.

example.q: Pointing to a boy, Meena says, "He is the son of my mother's only son." Who is the boy?

varieties.name: Direct statements
varieties.how: Put each statement into the family tree; note genders.

example.q: A is the son of B. B is the sister of C. How is C related to A?
steps: C is a sibling of B, gender not given.

varieties.name: Coded relations
varieties.how: Decode each symbol into a sentence, then draw the tree.

example.q: P + Q means P is the father of Q; P − Q means P is the wife of Q. What is A − B + C?
steps: A is the wife of B; B is the father of C.

tips: Mark gender only when it is clearly given; otherwise the answer may be "parent" or "cannot be determined".
In coded questions, write the decoded sentence under each symbol before drawing.
traps: "Only son of my father" can be the speaker himself.
Being someone's sibling does not tell you your gender.

questions.q: Pointing to a man, Rita said, "He is the son of my grandfather's only son." How is the man related to Rita?
questions.solution:
Rita's grandfather's only son = Rita's father.
The son of Rita's father = Rita's brother.

questions.q: A is the brother of B. B is the daughter of C. How is C related to A?
questions.solution:
B is the daughter of C, so C is B's parent.
A is B's brother, so C is also A's parent.
C's gender is not given, so C is A's father or mother.

questions.q:
P + Q means P is the father of Q; P − Q means P is the wife of Q; P × Q means P is the brother of Q; P ÷ Q means P is the daughter of Q.
If A + B × C − D, how is D related to A?
questions.solution:
A + B: A is the father of B.
B × C: B is the brother of C, so C is also A's child.
C − D: C is the wife of D, so C is A's daughter.
D is the husband of A's daughter = A's son-in-law.

questions.q: Introducing a woman, Raj said, "She is the wife of the only son of my father." How is the woman related to Raj?
questions.solution:
The only son of Raj's father is Raj himself.
So the woman is Raj's wife.

questions.q: In a family, P is the father of Q. Q is the mother of R and S. R is a boy and S is a girl. T is the brother of P. U is the wife of P. How is S related to U?
questions.solution:
U is the wife of P, and P is the father of Q, so Q is U's child.
S is Q's child, so S is U's grandchild.
S is a girl, so S is U's granddaughter.

questions.q:
A @ B means A is the mother of B; A # B means A is the husband of B; A $ B means A is the daughter of B; A % B means A is the brother of B.
If M % N @ O # P $ Q, how is M related to O?
questions.solution:
M % N: M is the brother of N.
N @ O: N is the mother of O.
So M is the brother of O's mother = O's maternal uncle.
(O # P $ Q only tells us about O's wife P and her parent Q.)
